source.title: To Cache or Not to Cache: Understanding and Mitigating Safety Incompatibility in Cross-Model KV Cache Reuse
source.authors: Zhi-Wei Lin; Jia-Hao Liu; Yan Liu; Cheng-Peng Wang

page_placements.theme: Model, adapter and cache composition can transmit or repair safety loss

record.tranche_reason: The study measures harmful-response behavior under cross-model KV-cache reuse, a distinct intervention and setting from the claim’s fine-tuning and first-token mechanisms.
record.gate_note: The study directly evaluates harmfulness and safety-score changes under cache reuse and value mapping. It does not test the listed fine-tuning, token-position, compliant-prefill, suffix, decoding, weight-localization, shallowness-cause, or deepening claims. No results are reported for those mechanisms.
record.test_reason: The study measures harmful-response rates when an instruct or LoRI receiver reuses prompt-prefix KV caches from a base or sibling sender model. This is a cache-level inference perturbation, not harmful or benign fine-tuning (V1/V2), per-token KL by response position (V3), or a compliant response opening, suffix or decoding change (V4). It also does not localize safety in weights (V5), explain shallowness (V6) or deepen alignment (V7). The original source Qi et al. 2023 is cited only as the source of HEx-PHI fitting prompts. Relation corrected from the reader's 'tests'/T3 to cites_only/T6.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct as paraphrased: cache reuse can change receiver safety in either direction, values matter more than keys, and VREPARO improves safety compatibility while retaining TTFT reductions, with trade-offs in benign refusal and QA quality.
record.recipe_differences: The study evaluates cross-model KV-cache reuse and offline affine mapping of reused values; it does not use the fine-tuning, token-position, or compliant-opening methods in the claim.
record.method_sensitivity: Safety outcomes vary with sender–receiver pair and reuse configuration; V-only reuse changes HarmBench ASR more than K-only reuse across all evaluated pairs, while full-KV effects can differ from V-only effects.

fits_no_version.finding: Reusing base-model (or sibling-adapter) prompt KV caches in an aligned receiver shifts HarmBench ASR and StrongREJECT scores in either direction. Examples: Llama-3-8B-Instruct V-only 5.80% to 57.25%; Qwen3-8B full KV 6.98% to 4.65%. Value reuse shifts ASR more than key reuse in all pairs.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Cross-model KV-cache reuse produces safety incompatibility in the receiver, with direction and size depending on the model pair and on whether keys or values are reused.

record.problems: The characterization results retain only prompts whose outputs pass the validity check in every compared condition; the authors note that these checks do not certify semantic validity and include retrospective Codex-assisted annotations rather than an independent human audit. The paper reports point estimates. Mitigation calibration uses XSTest refusal rates and does not ensure preservation of benign refusal rates on OR-Bench.
record.rows_left_out: Omitted native-referenced safety deviation metrics and benign-refusal results, which do not directly measure the harmful-response outcomes recorded here; also omitted QA and latency results. See Tables 3, 4, and 10.

untested.parts: No fine-tuning on harmful examples. The LoRI-D variants are pre-existing adapters on a base model, not safety-trained models attacked by fine-tuning.
No benign fine-tuning of a safety-aligned model. LoRI-D Code is trained from the non-aligned Llama-3-8B base, so its high native ASR is not erosion of prior safety.
No per-token KL or response-position analysis.
No prefilling, adversarial suffixes or decoding changes. Cache reuse alters prompt-prefix states, not the response opening.
No weight or rank localization of safety.
No analysis of why alignment is shallow.

record.verdict_notes: All rows correctly carry versions ['none']. One could argue a loose analogy to shallow alignment, since base-model states pushing an instruct model toward compliance resemble the base/aligned contrast. However, the paper makes no position-wise or response-opening analysis, so no version is tested. Reader's relation 'tests' and tranche T3 were overridden.

versions.untested_parts: Harmful fine-tuning on a few to a few hundred examples and its effect on refusal.
Benign-data fine-tuning and its effect on harmful compliance.
Per-token KL divergence between aligned and base models across response positions.
Compliant-opening prefills, adversarial suffixes, decoding changes, and whether passing the first response tokens causes bypass.
Whether a small set of model weights or ranks carries safety behavior. The study maps KV values, not model weights.
Whether the data or objective used in safety training causes shallowness.
Training safety beyond the first response tokens and testing whether the deeper behavior holds up.

relation.reason: Qi et al. (2023) is cited for HEx-PHI fitting examples; the shallow-safety findings are neither tested nor used as a method.

tranche.reason: The study measures safety changes from cross-model prompt-cache reuse and affine cache correction. It neither tests nor uses any of V1–V7.

source_check.notes: Table 2 uses prompts valid under all four conditions; its baselines differ from the full-reuse-only subsets in Tables 5–6. The authors’ conclusion paraphrase is accurate; cache values are activations, so their stronger effect does not establish localization in model parameters.
